label: History
value: Mrs. Agatha Sowerby spent many years in Brierley leading the Sewing Circle
unit: Mrs. Agatha Sowerby spent many years in Brierley leading the Sewing Circle, helping direct the Sunday school, and supporting the Church Aid Society and Foreign Missions Auxiliary. Her home situated at Sowerby's Hollow allowed her to observe everyone entering or leaving the community. When Obed Abernethy and Thirza Abernethy adopted Nell, Agatha was initially skeptical and disapproving. Soon after Nell's arrival, Agatha visited Grey Shutters and made frank remarks about Nell's red hair and freckles, sparking an outburst from the girl for which Nell later apologized. Over the years, Agatha continued her active participation in church and village matters, frequently offering unsought advice and managing community efforts. After her husband Thomas passed away following a long illness, Agatha faced financial difficulties due to a farm mortgage and high medical expenses. To avoid leaving Brierley, she accepted Thirza's offer to move into Grey Shutters, establishing her living quarters in the former spare room. She provided her handcrafted quilts to Nell and her roommates when they went to college.

label: Personality
value: Aunt Euphemia possesses a youthful outlook.
unit: Aunt Euphemia possesses a youthful outlook, a radiant smile, and an indulgent, cheerful nature. While candid about her past grudges, she considers holding ill feelings to be a waste of time as one ages.

label: History
value: Aunt Euphemia was left alone in a large house.
unit: Left alone in a large house after her single daughter departed for foreign mission work, Aunt Euphemia was invited to move to Portmaris to manage a rented house named Tabby's Place for college students Nell, Honora, Mabel, and Cressida. She arrived after the young women set up the house, bringing along her cats—the Sarah-cat and Joseph. Over the next three winters, she served as a housemother to the girls, keeping the home warm and welcoming visiting college friends with a cheerful, relaxed attitude. During the Christmas break, she chose to stay behind at Tabby's Place to tend to the house and care for the cats rather than leave them unattended. She frequently shared her practical wisdom and humor, offered advice on suitors and education, and observed the young women complete their college years. When the group prepared to disperse at graduation, Aunt Euphemia decided to adopt Smudge so that he could remain together with her other two cats.

label: History
value: Barney drives a double-seated buggy.
unit: Barney drives a double-seated buggy to Pale Sands along with his sister Odette to carry Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke to a concert. He harbors immense, silent admiration for Nell and takes great pride in driving her, though he sits quietly in a corner during events and speaks very little. He eventually asks his sister Odette to propose marriage to Nell on his behalf after his father bestows the upper farm upon him, offering to wait until she finishes college. Following Nell's firm refusal, Barney marries Nettie Scobie, a union favored by his mother, and their 'appearing out' takes place on a Sunday at church.

label: History
value: Belinda went to live at Echo Cottage at age thirteen.
unit: Belinda went to live at Echo Cottage at age thirteen in exchange for room, board, and clothing, following three of her sisters in service to Miss Rosalind. Because of her strong resemblance to her sisters, her mistress called her 'Belinda the Fourth' rather than her actual name, Leonora. She assisted Miss Rosalind in maintaining the stone dwelling and hosting imaginary tea parties until Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke arrived. She formed a deep admiration for Nell, often practicing in front of her mirror to copy Nell's graceful movements and speech. When Miss Rosalind grew frail and lonely, Belinda expressed great concern to Nell and helped orchestrate the reunion of Miss Rosalind and Stephen Stanhope. Following Miss Rosalind's wedding to Stephen, Belinda moved to Boston along with the couple and Cedric, though she initially experienced homesickness and missed St. Brendan's Island. She returned to Echo Cottage each summer with the Stanhopes, maintaining her warm friendship and affectionate devotion toward Nell.

value: Cedric moved from the United States to Brierley

Upon starting school, he immediately bonded with Nell, becoming fast friends and one of her favorite pupils. He frequently brought her flowers, shared his inner imaginative thoughts, and confided in her about his deceased mother and his father, Stephen Stanhope. When his father visited Brierley, Cedric joyfully reunited with him and mentioned traveling to Welby to see Miss Rosalind Penrose, helping spark the rekindling of Stephen and Rosalind's past romance. Following his father's marriage to Rosalind, Cedric welcomed her into his life as 'Mother Rosalind' and spent time residing in Boston with them while returning to Echo Cottage and Brierley during the summer months. As he grew into a sixteen-year-old youth, his early childhood play with imaginary 'Rock People' faded into growing tall and playing football, though his close friendship with Nell remained unchanged.

label: History
value: Cyril returned from Europe
unit: After returning from Europe to complete his Arts degree as a Junior at Wexcombe, Cyril met Nell Harcourt in a park during a rainstorm when his umbrella rescued hers. Impressed by her, he sent a dozen long-stemmed roses and a poem to her residence. Throughout their college years, he courted her with romantic gestures, sending her violets and sonnets for her birthday. He introduced his mother and sisters to the coeds at Tabby's Place, though he mistakenly gave them the wrong day for their arrival. label: History
value: Flossie Tulk attended school in Brierley
unit: Flossie Tulk attended school in Brierley under Mr. Pidgeon and later Miss Thorne. She frequently clashed with Nell Harcourt, famously daring her to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Pembroke's kitchen roof, which resulted in Nell falling and injuring her ankle. Flossie won the top prize for knitted lace at an exhibition and joined the Regent's entrance class alongside her peers. After passing the Entrance exam by a narrow margin, she moved on to the Academy for higher studies. Unlike many of her classmates who became teachers upon graduating, Flossie chose to return to Regent's for another year. Prior to Nell and Hugh's departure for college, a send-off celebration was held at the Tulk home, where Flossie displayed uncharacteristic friendliness despite continuing her sarcastic commentary.

label: History
value: Hugh spent three years in Alberta with his father.
unit: After spending three years in Alberta with his father, Hugh returned to Brierley to resume his schooling, quickly establishing himself at the top of his class and competing intensely with Nell Harcourt. His teasing of Nell by calling her 'Carrots' sparked a long-running grudge on her part, despite his immediate remorse and sincere apologies. He later saved Nell from the bridge piling in Gorham Pullen's dory and excelled in the Regent's class, ultimately winning the medalist honors while Nell won the Avery scholarship. To fund his own college education, he taught school in Pale Sands for a year and actively co-founded and led the Brierley Village Improvement Society as its president. He surrendered the Brierley school position to Nell so she could remain near home, which led to a reconciliation and the start of a warm friendship between them. At Wexcombe, Hugh led the Freshmen to victory in the Arts Rush, was elected Freshman Class President, and joined the Lambs fraternity. Although he courted Nell and eventually proposed to her, she declined his romantic advances, prompting him to step back into a distant, polite acquaintance. He pushed himself to academic extremes at university, earning High Honors in Classics and the Cooper Prize, but suffered a life-threatening case of typhoid fever that summer before recovering.

value: Isolde Pembroke resides at Pear Hill
unit: Isolde Pembroke resides at Pear Hill in Brierley. After returning home from visiting her aunt in Delford, she meets Nell Harcourt and the two girls become bosom friends, forming playhouses and sharing imaginative adventures. Their friendship survives a temporary ban imposed by her strict mother after an accidental intoxication incident with raspberry cordial. During a visit from her wealthy, stern aunt Miss Lavinia Pembroke, Isolde and Nell accidentally leap onto her bed in the dark, but Nell's bold confession placates Lavinia, securing music lessons for Isolde. Later, after a story writing club is formed, Isolde secretly submits Nell's story 'Evadne's Atonement' to a commercial contest, winning a twenty-five dollar prize for her friend. As she matures, Isolde becomes a member of the local Improvement Society. She eventually falls in love with Gideon Duckett and marries him in a grand traditional ceremony at Pear Hill, moving to his farm two miles away. Later, she gives birth to a son.

label: History
value: Mabel became one of Nell Harcourt's close companions.
unit: While studying at Regent's Academy, Mabel became one of Nell Harcourt's close companions, winning the Second Year beauty prize. Following her time at Regent's, she worked as a schoolteacher until deciding to resume her studies at Wexcombe. She proposed renting Tabby's Place in Wexcombe alongside Nell and Honora Hollis, bringing her Aunt Euphemia to handle housekeeping. During her time at university, she managed the household's financial records, struggled through periods of academic exhaustion alongside her roommates, and participated in the literary activities of the Philomathic Society. Upon finishing tests for her final year, she achieved a respectable overall performance at Convocation.

label: History
value: Nell Harcourt was born in Harborough, Nova Scotia.
unit: Born in Harborough, Nova Scotia to high school teacher Edmund Harcourt and his wife Bertha, Nell was orphaned at an early age. She was sent to St. Brendan's Island and adopted by Thirza at Grey Shutters after an adoption agency error. She grew up in Brierley, attending the local school where she formed a lifelong friendship with Isolde Pembroke and shared a tempestuous rivalry and eventual camaraderie with Hugh Carrow, whom she famously struck with a slate after he teased her about her red hair. After winning the Avery Scholarship at Regent's school, Nell deferred college to teach at the Brierley school for two years to assist Thirza. During her tenure, she helped reunite Miss Rosalind Irving with her long-lost love, Stephen Stanhope. Afterwards, Nell enrolled at Wexcombe college. While attending, her story 'Evadne's Atonement' won a baking powder contest prize when submitted by Isolde, and she later published work in The Youth's Friend. Over time, she declined romantic proposals from Barney Pullen, Hugh Carrow, and Cyril, remaining dedicated to her studies, her writing, and her affection for her home at Grey Shutters.

She grew up in Brierley, attending the local school where she formed a lifelong friendship with Isolde Pembroke and shared a tempestuous rivalry and eventual camaraderie with Hugh Carrow, whom she famously struck with a slate after he teased her about her red hair. After winning the Avery Scholarship at Regent's school, Nell deferred college to teach at the Brierley school for two years to assist Thirza. During her tenure, she helped reunite Miss Rosalind Irving with her long-lost love, Stephen Stanhope. Afterwards, Nell enrolled at Wexcombe college. While attending, her story 'Evadne's Atonement' won a baking powder contest prize when submitted by Isolde, and she later published work in The Youth's Friend. Over time, she declined romantic proposals from Barney Pullen, Hugh Carrow, and Cyril, remaining dedicated to her studies, her writing, and her affection for her home at Grey Shutters.

label: History
value: Obed Abernethy resided at Grey Shutters
unit: Obed Abernethy resided at Grey Shutters in Brierley with his sister Thirza. Seeking farm help due to his advancing age and heart trouble, he arranged to adopt an orphan boy. Upon driving to Alder River to meet the train, he discovered that an eleven-year-old girl, Nell Harcourt, had been sent by mistake instead. Unable to leave her behind, Obed brought Nell home and quickly grew fond of her chatter, advocating for her to stay. He quietly supported and indulged Nell, buying her a fashionable dress for Christmas despite his intense shyness in local stores. Over the years, he took immense pride in her academic and personal achievements. Obed unexpectedly passed away from his heart condition shortly after Nell won the Avery scholarship, leaving her and Thirza deeply grieving his loss.

Unable to leave her behind, Obed brought Nell home and quickly grew fond of her chatter, advocating for her to stay. He quietly supported and indulged Nell, buying her a fashionable dress for Christmas despite his intense shyness in local stores. Over the years, he took immense pride in her academic and personal achievements. Obed unexpectedly passed away from his heart condition shortly after Nell won the Avery scholarship, leaving her and Thirza deeply grieving his loss.

label: History
value: Odette attended Brierley school.
unit: Odette attended Brierley school alongside Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke, where she joined the local tale-writing society and wrote sensible, unromantic stories. She prepared for the Entrance exam, passed with steady composure, and attended Regent's Academy, earning top marks in domestic science. Upon graduating, she took a teaching position in Stonebridge, where she maintained order strictly and earned a place on the Inspector's Honor Roll. She later became a member of the Brierley Village Improvement Society and briefly took over teaching at Brierley school. During a winter holiday, she conveyed a proposal of marriage on behalf of her brother Barney to Nell Harcourt, which Nell refused. Odette subsequently left Brierley to teach on western prairies. Returning from the West, she married Mr. Inglis, a wealthy mining millionaire from Winnipeg, in a lavish Brierley ceremony.

value: > Me! Well, I am completely fine. Never in my entire existence have I felt superior to this. To be sure, I was somewhat weakened by that congestion during the previous winter. However, simply look at my complexion. Surely, I do not appear at all like a sick person.

label: Quotes
value: > Nell, the time is drawing near when I will be resting in that place. You, Isolde, and everyone else will be moving around, brimming with vitality—while I will be situated there—within the ancient cemetery—deceased!

label: Quotes
value: > And, oh, Nell—dying is not what I want. The thought of dying frightens me.

label: Quotes
value: > I want to live. I want to live the way other girls do. I—I desire to get married, Nell—and—and—possess tiny children. You are aware that babies were always something I loved, Nell. value: Opal Pettigrew grew up in Brierley.
unit: Opal Pettigrew grew up in Brierley and attended the local school, where she shared an aisle with Nell Harcourt and was part of the school's social circle. She joined Nell and Isolde in forming a tale-writing society, participated in games like acting out Elaine, and entered the Regent's class under Miss Thorne. After studying at the Academy in Regent's, she earned her teacher's license and took up a teaching position at the Delford school. Throughout her youth, she engaged in numerous flirtations and acquired many suitors, including Nelson Atkins, Wilbur Blair, Leonard Kimball, Varley Bell, and Herb Tranter. During the winter of her teaching years, she contracted a severe bout of congestion that developed into galloping consumption. Though she initially concealed her illness and insisted she would resume teaching, she steadily weakened and was forced to give up her work. She spent her final summer at home in Brierley, sharing poignant conversations about life and death with Nell. Opal passed away peacefully in her sleep shortly thereafter, and was buried in the Brierley church cemetery.

Following the death of Nutmeg during a lightning storm, Mr. Pettifer's estranged wife Emily arrived unexpectedly, prompting a reconciliation between the couple. With Emily managing the household, Mr. Pettifer became a tidier, more socially engaged neighbor, regularly attending church and contributing to village affairs. During Nell's pursuits as an author, he offered blunt yet constructive literary critiques and practical guidance.

label: History
value: Mr. Pidgeon was the schoolmaster at Brierley school
unit: During his tenure as the schoolmaster at Brierley school, Mr. Pidgeon focused much of his attention on preparing older students for entrance exams while spending considerable time courting Sukey Pullen. He administered harsh punishments to students, forcing Nell Harcourt to stand on the dais after she broke a slate over Hugh Carrow's head, and later making her sit next to Hugh as a penalty for being late. His uneven discipline led to complaints, including an incident where Sam Gammon's father confronted him after Sam was caned. At a local concert, he delivered Mark Antony's address while looking toward Sukey. At the conclusion of the school term in June, he delivered an emotional parting speech with tears in his eyes before relinquishing his position, which was later taken by Miss Thorne.

value: Rosalind is romantic.
unit: Rosalind is romantic, imaginative, and youthful in spirit, frequently engaging in lighthearted play and pretending. Despite her whimsical nature and love of solitude, she is deeply practical, hospitable, and warm-hearted. She despises the thought of advancing in age and resists social expectations of conventional old maidenhood. She possesses a voice that evokes satin, splashing water, and fairy bells.

One autumn day, Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke stumbled upon Echo Cottage and struck up a delightful acquaintance with her and her handmaiden, Belinda the Fourth. Nell quickly became a close friend and kindred spirit, visiting frequently to share in imaginative games, tea parties, and talks. Through Nell, Rosalind met Cedric Stanhope, the son of her former fiancé Stephen Stanhope, and formed a warm maternal bond with the young boy. After Stephen Stanhope returned to the area and sent word through Nell that he wished to see her, he visited Echo Cottage, leading to their reconciliation. They were married in late August beneath the garden's honeysuckle trellis—the exact spot where Stephen had proposed twenty-five years earlier—and departed for Boston and a trip to the Pacific coast. They continue to return to Echo Cottage each summer with Cedric and Belinda the Fourth to enjoy the season.

label: History
value: Thirza Abernethy spent her youth residing at Grey Shutters.
unit: Thirza Abernethy spent her quiet, restricted youth and middle age residing with her brother Obed at their secluded farmstead, Grey Shutters. Intending to adopt a young orphan boy to assist on the farm, she and Obed mistakenly received Nell Harcourt, a young girl, from the asylum. Though initially stunned by the mistake, Thirza allowed Nell to stay on trial and quickly grew deeply attached to her, taking on the responsibility of her upbringing, education, and spiritual guidance. Following the death of her brother Obed, Thirza considered selling Grey Shutters due to grief and failing eyes, but chose to stay when Nell gave up a university scholarship to remain with her. As her vision improved and her sharp nature softened, she welcomed Mrs. Agatha Sowerby into her home to live together and took in the orphaned twins, Robin and Lucy Farrow.

label: History
value: Miss Agnes Thorne became the first female teacher in Brierley.
unit: Miss Agnes Thorne became the first female teacher employed in Brierley. She introduced interactive learning routines, including Friday recitations, nature 'field' days, and daily physical culture exercises. In November, she led the school in organizing a Christmas Night concert to raise funds for a schoolhouse flag. Though she received an offer to teach at a grade school in her home district, she chose to stay in Brierley to guide her students through their Regent's entrance examinations. She organized an after-school preparation class for her proficient pupils, including Nell Harcourt, Odette Pullen, Opal Pettigrew, Wilfred Mott, Elias Purdy, and Flossie Tulk. At the end of two years, her term in Brierley concluded, but all her Entrance class candidates successfully passed their examinations. In later years, she maintained a close relationship with Nell Harcourt and visited Grey Shutters as a guest.
